'''Blue Line 1''' is a [[rapid transit]] metro line of the [[Mumbai Metro]], in the city of [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. The {{Cvt|11.40|km}} line is fully elevated and consists of 12 stations, from [[Versova metro station|Versova]] to [[Ghatkopar metro station|Ghatkopar]]. The line connects the [[Eastern Suburbs (Mumbai)|eastern]] and [[Western Suburbs (Mumbai)|western]] suburbs of Mumbai.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_mumbais-first-metro-may-chug-in-march-2013_1685026|title=Mumbai's first metro may chug in March 2013 |newspaper=[[DNA India]] |date=6 May 2012 |access-date=12 June 2012}}</ref> It was built at an estimated cost of {{INRConvert|4321|c}} and is operated by the Metro One Operation Pvt. Ltd (MOOPL) on a 5-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metros-construction-cost-goes-up-by-Rs-1500-crore-fare-may-rise/articleshow/18456097.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130225054920/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-02-12/mumbai/37057955_1_metro-fare-bus-fare-fare-hike|url-status=live|archive-date=25 February 2013|title=Metro's construction cost goes up by Rs 1500 crore, fare may rise |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date=12 February 2013 |access-date=12 February 2013}}</ref> This special purpose vehicle, namely, Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (Mumbai Metro 1), was incorporated for the implementation of the project. [[Reliance Infrastructure]] holds 74% of the equity share capital of MMOPL, 26% is with the [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority]] (MMRDA).<ref name="owner" />

The Mumbai Metro 1 Blue Line started operations on 8 June 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Maharashtra-CM-Prithivraj-Chavan-flags-off-Mumbai-Metro/articleshow/36238569.cms|title=Maharashtra CM Prithviraj Chavan flags off Mumbai Metro | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=8 June 2014 }}</ref> It has the eighth-highest passenger density of any metro line in the world.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/metro-breaches-25cr-passenger-mark-in-record-time/articleshow/57088665.cms|title=Mumbai Metro rail: Mumbai Metro breaches 25cr passenger mark in record time | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=11 February 2017 }}</ref> The Blue Line has the steepest curve of any metro line in India. There are a total of 64 curves on the line, with the steepest curve being {{Convert|107|m}}.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mumbai Metro uses RFID lubrication system to improve wheel maintenance|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-mumbai-metro-uses-rfid-lubrication-system-to-improve-wheel-maintenance-2336958|website=DNA India|access-date=28 February 2017|date=27 February 2017}}</ref>

==History==

===Background===
The [[Government of Maharashtra]] through the MMRDA, in order to improve the traffic and transportation scenario in Mumbai and to cater to the future travel needs in the next 2-3 decades began exploring the viability of various alternative mass transit systems which are efficient, economically viable and environment friendly. In this context, a detailed feasibility study was carried out under Indo-German technical co-operation by entrusting the consultancy work to Tewet in association with DE-Consult GmbH and [[Tata Consultancy Services]], during 1997–2000. The study recommended a mass transit corridor from [[Andheri]] to [[Ghatkopar]] as potentially bankable and economically viable, after examining a number of alternative corridors and alignments. This study was updated by the MMRDA in May 2004. Meanwhile, the [[Delhi Metro Rail Corporation]] (DMRC) prepared the master plan for Mumbai Metro, wherein they recommended extending the Andheri-Ghatkopar section to [[Versova, Mumbai|Versova]] as part of the master plan and identified it as a priority corridor for implementation. The State Government declared the project as a "public vital infrastructure project" and designated the MMRDA as the Project Implementation Agency (PIA).<ref name="mmrda1">{{cite web|url=http://202.54.119.40/projects_metro_rail.htm |title=Mmrda – Projects – Mumbai Metro Rail Project |website=Mmrda mumbai.org |access-date = 12 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319164955/http://202.54.119.40/projects_metro_rail.htm |archive-date=19 March 2012 }}</ref> The Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor was chosen as the first line in the master plan to be implemented.

The [[Mumbai Suburban Railway]] connects Mumbai from north to south. However, east–west connectivity is poor. The Versova-Ghatkopar route had no suburban rail link and was serviced by either BEST buses, autos or taxis.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/west/story/mumbai-metro-starts-public-route-price-196069-2014-06-08|title=Mumbai Metro opens for public, row erupts over ticket prices|agency=IANS |date=June 8, 2014 |magazine=India Today}}</ref> Blue Line provides east–west rail connectivity between the [[Eastern Suburbs (Mumbai)|Eastern]] and [[Western Suburbs (Mumbai)|Western]] suburbs of Mumbai.<ref name="TOI1">{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-dress-rehearsal-sees-7-trains-on-tracks/articleshow/26982942.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211062319/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-12-07/mumbai/44904119_1_passenger-several-trains-signal-system |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-12-11 |title=Metro dress rehearsal sees 7 trains on tracks |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=2013-12-07 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> It facilitates interchange between the Mumbai Suburban Railway and Mumbai Metro at [[Andheri railway station|Andheri]] and [[Ghatkopar railway station|Ghatkopar]] stations. The line significantly reduces the journey time from [[Versova (Mumbai)|Versova]] to Ghatkopar from 90–120 minutes to 21 minutes, and bypasses about 45 traffic signals.<ref name="livemint.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Politics/jgQox7qqUnR5siYQngF1tM/Mumbai-to-get-modern-metro-rail-from-Sunday.html|title=Mumbai Metro services to start on Sunday amid tariff dispute|first=Makarand Gadgil, P R.|last=Sanjai|date=7 June 2014|website=Livemint}}</ref> It also provides rail connectivity to the [[MIDC]] and [[SEEPZ]].<ref name="Reference A">{{cite web|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/seven-years-after-pm-laid-its-foundation-mumbais-first-metro-corridor-is-yet-to-see-the-light-of-day/1164130/0 |title=Seven years after PM laid its foundation, Mumbai's first Metro corridor is yet to see the light of day |work=The Indian Express |date=2013-09-04 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref>

The concession agreement for the Versova–Andheri–Ghatkopar corridor was signed with Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL), a joint venture company owned by [[Reliance Infrastructure]] (69%), [[Veolia Transport]] (5%) and the MMRDA (26%), in March 2007.<ref name="financialexpress1">{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/no-respite-for-mumbai-metro-as-project-cost-jumps-by-70-per-cent/1245850 |title=No respite for Mumbai Metro as project cost jumps by 70 per cent |work=The Financial Express |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref><ref name="indianexpress.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/now-mmopl-changes-track-says-metro-will-roll-in-dec/1168000/0 |title=Now, MMOPL changes track, says Metro will roll in Dec |work=[[The Indian Express]] |date=2013-09-12 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> SSRI Creative Infrastructure (Choksi Group) was the main technical contractor.<ref name="Ashley D'Mello">{{cite news|author=Ashley D'Mello |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Work-on-Metro-VAG-line-on-track/articleshow/6160998.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928192623/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-07-13/mumbai/28275673_1_metro-rail-bridge-andheri-station-rail-work |url-status=live |archive-date=28 September 2013 |title=Work on Metro VAG line on track |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=13 July 2010 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Manmohan Singh]] laid the foundation stone on 21 June 2006. The work order for the project was issued on 21 January 2008,<ref name="gulfnews.com">{{cite web|author=Pamela Raghunath |url=http://gulfnews.com/news/world/india/more-delays-in-mumbai-metro-1.1287566 |title=More delays in Mumbai metro |website=Gulf News |date=6 February 2014 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref> and work began on 8 February 2008.<ref name="Ashley D'Mello" /> In September 2011, MMOPL officials claimed that trial runs on the first section of the corridor, the {{Cvt|3|km}} Versova–[[D N Nagar metro station|D.N. Nagar]]–[[Azad Nagar metro station|Azad Nagar]] stretch, would start by February 2012, with a view to opening the stretch to commuters by March or April 2012.<ref><!--Old URL http://www.hindustantimes.com/3-km-of-Metro-Phase-I-to-be-ready-by-March-2012/Article1-748670.aspx-->Shaikh, Zeeshan. "[https://web.archive.org/web/20111126160119/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/3-km-of-Metro-Phase-I-to-be-ready-by-March-2012/Article1-748670.aspx 3 km of Metro Phase I to be ready by March 2012]." ''[[Hindustan Times]]''. 22 September 2011. Retrieved 22 September 2011.</ref> The deadline for completion of Blue line has been shifted several times. The following months have all, at some point of time, been announced as the deadline for completion of the project - July and September 2010, July 2011, March and November 2012,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/mumbais-metro-gets-a-sixth-deadline-for-completion-1.1154394|title=Mumbai's Metro gets a sixth deadline for completion|website=Gulf News|date=5 March 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-metro-likely-to-miss-its-august-deadline-1807774|title=Metro likely to miss its August deadline|first=Ateeq|last=Shaikh|date=6 March 2013|website=DNA India}}</ref> September 2013 (Phase 1: Versova to [[Airport Road metro station|Airport Road]]) and December 2013 (Phase 2: Airport Road to Ghatkopar),<ref name="gulfnews.com" /><ref name="The Times of India">{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Approach-roads-to-Metro-stations-not-yet-ready-RTI/articleshow/29965450.cms |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140208192653/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2014-02-07/mumbai/47125677_1_metro-phase-i-metro-stations-mumbai-metro |url-status=live |archive-date=2014-02-08 |title=Approach roads to Metro stations not yet ready: RTI |date=2014-02-07 |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref> and 31 March 2014.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mumbai-metro-enters-final-leg-safety-certs-likely-in-february-1948464 |title=Mumbai Metro enters final leg, safety certs likely in February |publisher=DNA |date=2014-01-10 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref>

The MMOPL blamed the delay in construction on the MMRDA. RInfra officials said that the MMRDA had to acquire land along the route and provide [[Right-of-way (transportation)|right of way]] to the MMOPL by December 2008.<ref name="ROW">{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/mosque-agrees-to-raze-minaret-in-way-of-bridge/1016830|title=Mosque agrees to raze minaret in way of bridge - Indian Express|website=The Indian Express}}</ref> As of August 2008, the MMRDA had only freed up 20% of required land. The lack of maps of underground utilities made the task more difficult. As per the contract between the MMOPL and the MMRDA, the MMRDA was supposed to hand over complete right of way to the MMOPL by mid-2008. The MMOPL eventually received nearly 100% of the land required for the project in December 2011, with the exceptions of the [[minaret]] of a mosque near [[Andheri metro station|Andheri station]] and a portion of the roof of [[Maheshwar Temple]] near [[Jagruti Nagar metro station|Jagruti Nagar station]] that still needed to be demolished.<ref name="ROW" /> Both impediments were resolved in October 2012 and the MMRDA finally obtained 100% right of way along the entire alignment of Blue Line.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/all-clear-for-versovaandherighatkopar-metro/1017650/0|title=All clear for Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar Metro - Indian Express|website=The Indian Express}}</ref>

By October 2011, the majority of the corridor's track-support pillars and girders had been laid, and the 12 individual stations were 70% complete, with most of the stations rising above platform level.<ref name="ToI70">[https://web.archive.org/web/20130928033938/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-10-11/mumbai/30266316_1_pillars-metro-rail-mmopl "Metro first line hinges on Andheri bridge"]. ''[[The Times of India]]'', 11 October 2011. Retrieved 2011-10-18.</ref> However, land acquisition and right-of-way issues, along with problems with the construction of a Metro-related viaduct, delayed the line's predicted completion to summer 2012.<ref name="ToI70" /><ref>[http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_work-on-metro-pillar-between-railway-tracks-begins-at-slow-pace_1600577 "Work on metro pillar between railway tracks begins at slow pace"]. ''Daily News and Analysis'', 19 October 2011. Retrieved 2011-10-26.</ref> In May 2012, the [[Indian Bank]] restructured the Mumbai Metro's {{INRConvert|1.08|b}} loan account, citing the project's land use problems.<ref name="Loan2012">{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/indian-bank-rejigs-mumbai-metro-loan-account/950689/1|title=Indian Bank rejigs Mumbai Metro loan account|work=The Financial Express|date=18 May 2012|access-date=23 May 2012}}</ref>

On 1 May 2013, a successful {{Cvt|2|km}} trial run from Versova to Azad Nagar stations was conducted on Blue Line in the presence of [[List of Chief Ministers of Maharashtra|Chief Minister]] [[Prithviraj Chavan]],<ref name="hindustantimes.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Metro-trial-run-from-Versova-to-Airport-Road-successful/Article1-1070601.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606022634/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/mumbai/Metro-trial-run-from-Versova-to-Airport-Road-successful/Article1-1070601.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 June 2013 |title=Metro trial run from Versova to Airport Road successful |work=[[Hindustan Times]] |date=4 June 2013 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> who said that the line would open to the public from September 2013.<ref name="VersGhatTrial">[https://web.archive.org/web/20130504095821/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-05-01/mumbai/38957142_1_versova-ghatkopar-mumbai-metro-metropolitan-region-development-authority "Mumbai Metro trial run successful"]. ''The Times of India''. 1 May 2013. Retrieved 5 June 2013.</ref><ref name="TrialRunNDTV2013">[http://www.ndtv.com/article/cities/mumbai-metro-trial-run-with-train-draped-in-flowers-361185 "Mumbai Metro: trial run with train draped in flowers"]. NDTV.com. 1 May 2013. Retrieved 5 June 2013.</ref> However, MMRDA officials told ''[[Business Standard]]'' in August 2013 that the metro would be delayed further as it had not received approval from the Central Railway Safety Commissioner, and some of the facilities remained incomplete.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/mumbai-metro-project-commissioning-further-delayed-113081300900_1.html |title=Mumbai Metro project commissioning further delayed |work=[[Business Standard]] |date=2013-08-15 |access-date=2014-02-06|last1=Jog |first1=Sanjay }}</ref> The first major trial run on Blue Line, began at 6:45pm IST on 3 June 2013 from [[Versova metro station]], and covered the {{Cvt|2|km}} stretch to [[Airport Road metro station]] by 7:05pm, according to MMRDA additional commissioner S.V.R. Srinivas, who was on board the train. Trial runs had been conducted for the past month, the most notable being the trial run on 1 May 2013, that was officially flagged off by the Chief Minister.<ref name="hindustantimes.com" /> However, trials prior to the 3 June trial, were restricted to the {{Convert|3|km}} between [[Versova metro station|Versova]] and [[Azad Nagar metro station|Azad Nagar]] stations on JP Road.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-trial-run-passes-7km-from-Versova-to-Andheri/articleshow/20418852.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130625185742/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-06-04/mumbai/39739933_1_svr-srinivas-andheri-station-metropolitan-region-development-authority |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-06-25 |title=Metro trial run passes 7 km from Versova to Andheri |date=2013-06-04 |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref>
 
Several tests were conducted before the metro opened to the public.<ref name="TOI1" /> According to the information given by the MMRDA to a [[Right to Information Act]] (RTI) query filed by activist Anil Galgali, around 5% of the civil works of the line were still pending as of December 2013. The reply to the RTI query said that Versova, D.N. Nagar, Azad Nagar, Chakala (J. B. Nagar) and Airport Road stations were 99% complete as of December 2013. Andheri, Saki Naka, Marol and Western Express Highway stations were in the range of 95-98%. Construction work at Ghatkopar was 90% complete, Asalpha and Jagruti Nagar stations were 80% and 85% complete respectively.<ref>{{cite web |author= |date=2014-02-07 |title=5% of metro work still pending in Mumbai |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-5-of-metro-work-still-pending-in-mumbai-1959899 |access-date=2014-03-27 |publisher=Daily News & Analysis (DNA)}}</ref>

The MMRDA sent a letter to [[Reliance Infrastructure|RInfra]] on 31 December 2013, asking them to change the name of the metro system from Reliance Metro to Mumbai Metro. B. ==== Accidents ====
Eight accidents occurred during the construction of Blue Line. In total, 2 people were killed and 21 injured during the construction of the line. The first accident occurred in May 2008 when 1 person was killed and another injured, when a pile rig collapsed at a construction site in Andheri (West). In 2009, 4 people were injured, when a steel reinforcement cage and temporary scaffolding of a concrete pillar caved in it Andheri (East). In April 2012, a crane at a construction site in Ghatkopar, veered off a truck and crashed on a portion of the nearby Sarvodaya Hospital. No one was injured as the affected portion of the hospital building was empty at the time.<ref>[http://dailypioneer.com/nation/92481-mumbai-metro-bridge-slab-collapse-1-killed-11-injured.html Mumbai Metro bridge slab collapse; 1 killed, 11 injured]</ref>

On 5 September 2012, a slab collapsed at the under-construction Subhash Nagar metro station in [[Andheri]], killing one construction worker and injuring 16 people.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120906164601/http://ibnlive.in.com/news/mumbai-metro-bridge-pillar-collapses-1-dead-10-injured/288421-3-237.html Mumbai: Metro bridge pillar collapses, 1 dead, 10 injured- Maharashtra- India-IBNLive]</ref> Following the incident, construction work on the metro was suspended. MMOPL fined the contractor, [[Hindustan Construction Company]], {{INRConvert|10|l|year=2012|nolink=yes}}.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131005230407/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Metro-officials-appoint-Geneva-firm-for-safety-at-construction-site/Article1-928412.aspx Metro officials appoint Geneva firm for safety at construction site - Hindustan Times]</ref> On 11 September 2012, MMOPL appointed Geneva-based SGS Consultants as independent safety consultants for the construction of Blue Line. Construction resumed on 25 September 2012, under the supervision of SGS Consultants, after the consultant submitted its preliminary report to the MMOPL.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/3-weeks-after-mishap-metro-elevated-corridor-work-restarts/1008468|title=3 weeks after mishap, Metro elevated corridor work restarts - Indian Express|website=The Indian Express}}</ref> The consultant remained with the project until the completion of Blue Line to help prevent future accidents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/swiss-firm-to-help-prevent-metro-mishaps/1001360/|title=Swiss firm to help prevent Metro mishaps - Indian Express|website=The Indian Express}}</ref>

According to SVR Srinivas, then additional metropolitan commissioner at MMRDA, "The accident was basically due to voids in the support. The support weakened due to rain and utilities underneath created voids. So, it was basically due to loosening of the soil due to construction activity and its erosion due to heavy rain that the support weakened. If because of any reason a part of the support settles, stress increases on the staging and causes it to fail leading to a cascading effect".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/one-dead-but-mmrda-panel-blames-mumbai-metro-mishap-on-natural-reasons/1022224|title=One dead, but MMRDA panel blames Mumbai Metro mishap on 'natural reasons' - Indian Express|website=The Indian Express}}</ref>

===Opening===
The first metro service was flagged off by Maharashtra Chief Minister Prithviraj Chavan, along with Reliance Infra Chairman Anil Ambani and wife Tina Ambani, on 8 June 2014 at 10:10 am from Versova station. Chavan's appearance at the inauguration came despite the fact that he had threatened to boycott the ceremony the previous day to protest RInfra's decision to raise fares.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-gets-its-first-metro-prithviraj-chavan-flags-off-operations-from-versova/|title=Mumbai gets its first metro; Prithviraj Chavan flags off operations from Versova|date=8 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/chavan-flags-off-metro-service-114060800522_1.html|title=Chavan flags off Metro service|author=BS Reporter|date=9 June 2014|work=Business Standard}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/newswire/story/prithviraj-chavan-launches-mumbai-metro/843663|title=Prithviraj Chavan Launches Mumbai Metro|website=outlookindia.com/}}</ref> The line was scheduled to open to the public at 12:10pm, with the first service departing from Ghatkopar station. This was delayed by 10 minutes and departed at 12:20 pm. The train was further delayed by nearly half an hour, as it had to halt beyond the planned [[terminal dwell time|dwell time]] at certain stations due to a technical glitch.<ref name=autogenerated4>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-hit-by-technical-glitch-on-debut-trains-running-late/articleshow/36246251.cms|title=Mumbai Metro hit by technical glitch on debut, trains running late | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=8 June 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/140607/business-latest/article/mumbai-metro-will-be-thrown-open-mumbaikars-tomorrow|title=Mumbai Metro faces technical glitch on first day|date=7 June 2014|website=Deccan Chronicle}}</ref> This in turn caused some other trains to also be delayed by 20–30 minutes.<ref name=autogenerated4 /><ref name=autogenerated5>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Technical-snag-stops-Mumbai-Metro-comes-as-last-straw-after-crowds-of-weekend-revellers-overwhelm-citys-newest-ride/articleshow/36565093.cms|title=Technical snag stops Mumbai Metro, comes as last straw after crowds of weekend revellers overwhelm city's newest ride | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=15 June 2014 }}</ref>

MMOPL announced a special introductory fare of {{INR}} 10, regardless of distance, for the first 30 days of service.<ref name="livemint.com" /> The authority also announced that children under the age of 12 years and/or up to four feet tall, and accompanied by their parents, could travel for free on opening weekend.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-metro-announces-free-weekend-joyride-for-u-12-children/15377170|title=Mumbai Metro announces free weekend joyride for u-12 children|date=13 June 2014|website=mid-day}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated5 /> On opening day, the line ran for 11 hours, and carried 2.40 lakh commuters. The second day, which saw the line operated for its entire 18.5-hour schedule, saw 2.97 lakh commuters use the line. Blue Line had transported 1 million passengers by 4:30 p.m. on 11 June or within 59 operating hours; reaching the milestone quicker than any other Indian metro system.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Million-mark-for-Mumbai-Metro-on-just-4th-day/articleshow/36404198.cms|title=Million mark for Mumbai Metro on just 4th day | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=11 June 2014 }}</ref> In the first week of operations, 21.56 lakh commuters travelled on the line, at an average of 3.08 lakh daily.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-ferries-20-lakh-commuters-in-first-week/articleshow/36618106.cms|title=Mumbai Metro ferries 20 lakh commuters in first week | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=15 June 2014 }}</ref> Within days of the metro's opening, many commuters switched from using BEST buses and autos. Authorities estimated a 25% reduction in BEST commuters along the route as a result of the metro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-metro-effect-best-loses-11000-commuters-a-day/15370191|title=Mumbai Metro effect: BEST loses 11,000 commuters a day|date=11 June 2014|website=mid-day}}</ref> Ticket sales on BEST Bus Route Number 340, the most popular bus route between Andheri and Ghatkopar, dropped by {{INR}} 1.5 lakh in the first three days of Blue Line's opening.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-cuts-BEST-yield-by-Rs-1-5-lakh/articleshow/36404215.cms|title=Metro cuts BEST yield by Rs 1.5 lakh | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=12 June 2014 }}</ref>

===2014-17===
In its first year of operation, from June 2014 to June 2015, Blue Line transported over 92 million commuters, and made over 130,000 trips, covering a distance of over {{Cvt|1400000|km|4=0}}. The line carried an average of 263,000 commuters on weekdays. The MMOPL earned a total revenue of {{INRConvert|136|c|nolink=yes}}, and incurred losses of {{INRConvert|191|c|nolink=yes}}. The revenues include {{INRConvert|13.1|c|nolink=yes}} earned through leasing station space to 52 stalls across its 12 stations. The MMOPL said that it incurred an expenditure of {{INRConvert|55|l|nolink=yes}} per day to maintain the system and car depot.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/mumbai-metro-branding-on-track-115061001174_1.html|title=Mumbai Metro: Branding on track|first=Sanjay|last=Jog|date=10 June 2015|work=Business Standard}}</ref> On 4 June 2015, metro authorities announced that Blue Line had transported 100 million passengers since operations began.<ref name=autogenerated3>{{Cite web|url=https://www.railwaygazette.com/mumbai-metro-passes-100-million-in-a-year/40970.article|title=Mumbai Metro passes 100 million in a year|website=Railway Gazette International}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web|url=https://www.railjournal.com/passenger/metros/mumbai-metro-ridership-reaches-100-million/|title=Mumbai metro ridership reaches 100 million|date=5 June 2015}}</ref>

Mumbai Metro One announced that Blue Line had transported more than 150 million passengers since operations began, crossing the milestone on 26 January 2016, India's 67th Republic Day.<ref name=autogenerated2>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/mumbai-news/mumbai-metro-crosses-150-million-riders-1273027|title=Mumbai Metro Crosses 150 Million Riders|website=NDTV.com}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated7>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-metro-crosses-150-million-ridership-mark/16919183|title=Mumbai Metro crosses 150 million ridership mark|date=3 February 2016|website=mid-day}}</ref> Blue Line transported 200 million passengers within 786 days of operations. It crossed the 250 million mark on 11 February, or within 957 days, the fastest time in which any metro in India has reached the milestone.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite news|title=Mumbai Metro breaches 25cr passenger mark in record time - Times of India|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/metro-breaches-25cr-passenger-mark-in-record-time/articleshow/57088665.cms|website=The Times of India|date=11 February 2017 |access-date=12 February 2017}}</ref>
[[File:Mumbai_Line_1_metro_rake.jpg|thumb|Metro rake approaching [[Andheri metro station|Andheri]] station in 2019]] In 2017, Mumbai Metro One partnered with [[Google]] to integrate metro details into [[Google Maps]]. This collaboration enabled users to access authentic timetables and geographic information for the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar route. Trip timings, with frequencies of four minutes during peak hours and eight minutes during non-peak hours, were provided. Google Maps also displayed facilities like stairs, escalators, and ticket counters, helping commuters plan their journeys more efficiently.<ref name=googlemapspartnership>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gadgets360.com/apps/news/google-maps-now-features-mumbai-metro-details-1707154|title=Mumbai Metro Details Now Available on Google Maps|date=2 June 2016|website=gadgets-360.com}}</ref>

==Finances==

===Construction cost===
The original estimated cost of constructing Blue Line was {{INRConvert|2356|c|year=2007}} when the contract was signed in March 2007.<ref name="financialexpress.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/no-respite-for-mumbai-metro-as-project-cost-jumps-by-70-per-cent/1245850/0 |title=No respite for Mumbai Metro as project cost jumps by 70 per cent |work=The Financial Express |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> However, delays increased the cost by 84% over six years, and the project cost was {{INRConvert|4321|c|nolink=yes}}.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/1882626/report-mumbai-metro-ride-is-going-to-be-an-expensive-one |title=Mumbai Metro ride is going to be an expensive one |publisher=DNA |date=2013-09-01 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceB">{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-yet-to-move-fares-move-northwards/Article1-1117620.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130906003741/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-yet-to-move-fares-move-northwards/Article1-1117620.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 September 2013 |title=Mumbai Metro yet to move, fares move northwards |work=Hindustan Times |date=5 September 2013 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref>

To offset the escalation, RInfra-led MMOPL asked for a 130-150% increase in fares.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mmrda-seeks-itemised-break-up-and-reasons-for-metro-cost-escalation/ |title=MMRDA seeks itemised break-up and reasons for Metro cost escalation |work=The Indian Express |date=2014-02-06 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref> An MMOPL spokesperson said, "The principal reason for an increase is the inability of MMRDA to provide 100 per cent unencumbered RoW, which was contractually committed by MMRDA to be handed over to MMOPL on or before September 2007. The increase in fares is necessitated due to an increase in operating costs, owing to a steep increase in all economic indices; inflation, interest rate, foreign exchange, etc. These factors have also increased the estimated project cost." However, the MMRDA denied the request stating that the cost escalation of the project and the fare hike demand were separate issues. An MMRDA official told ''Business Standard'', "There is no question of any fare hike right now, as the issue will be considered after the service is started by MMOPL. The rise in capital expenditure will not impact fares immediately."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/no-immediate-fare-rise-for-mumbai-metro-declares-mmrda-114011600840_1.html |title=No immediate fare rise for Mumbai metro, declares MMRDA |work=Business Standard |date=2014-01-18 |access-date=2014-03-27|last1=Jog |first1=Sanjay }}</ref>

MMOPL completed the refinancing of project borrowings, achieving substantial benefits through extension of maturity and reduction of interest costs in June 2015. With this refinancing, the final repayment of {{INRConvert|1650|c|nolink=yes}} on the loans has been extended to the year 2037. The interest rate stands reduced from 13% to 11.75% per annum, and the average maturity period of loans has almost doubled to 14 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/rinfras-mumbai-metro-refinances-1650cr-debt/article7306234.ece|title=RInfra's Mumbai Metro refinances ₹1,650-cr debt|website=@businessline|date=11 June 2015 }}</ref>

===Dispute over initial fare===
The state government announced in 2004 that the fare as per 2003-04 levels was fixed as {{INR}} 6 up to {{Cvt|3|km}}, {{INR}} 8 for {{Cvt|3-8|km}} and {{INR}} 10 beyond {{Cvt|8|km}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/cm-okays-metro-fare-with-max-slab-of-rs-13/1164749/0 |title=CM okays Metro fare with max slab of Rs 13 |work=The Indian Express |date=2013-09-05 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> The originally agreed tariff hike schedule until 2042–43, based on the fare formula of 1.5 times the BEST fare, provided for an 11% hike after every three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Maharashtra-seeks-explanation-for-Metro-fare-hike-demand/articleshow/22528465.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928192627/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-09-13/mumbai/42040234_1_mmopl-fare-hike-demand-fare-revision |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-09-28 |title=Maharashtra seeks explanation for Metro fare hike demand |date=2013-09-13 |work=[[The Times of India]] |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> On 6 June 2013, the MMRDA said that MMOPL had asked for the fares for Blue Line be increased by more than 50%, even though the metro had not yet been opened.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/mumbai/others/No-ones-ridden-metro-yet-but-operator-wants-50-fare-hike/articleshow/20468561.cms|title=No one's ridden metro yet, but operator wants 50% fare hike|work=Mumbai Mirror|date=7 June 2013|access-date=7 July 2013}}</ref> On 5 September 2013, the Chief Minister approved a revision of fares to between {{INR}} 9 and {{INR}} 13.<ref name="dnaindia6">{{cite web|author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-steep-hike-in-fare-likely-1983855 |title=Steep hike in fare likely |website=Daily News and Analysis |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> The notification allowed for fares to be raised by 11% every four years.<ref>{{cite news|agency=Press Trust of India |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/mumbai-metro-may-start-soon-as-reliance-infrastructure-allowed-to-fix-fares/articleshow/34437924.cms |title=Mumbai Metro may start soon as Reliance Infrastructure allowed to fix fares |work=The Economic Times |date=2014-04-30 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

On 11 September 2013, the MMOPL said that the metro would commence operations in December 2013, regardless of whether or not the fare increase was granted.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/mumbai/others/Metro-1-will-be-ready-by-year-end-MMOPL/articleshow/22495271.cms |title=Metro 1 will be ready by year-end: MMOPL |work=Mumbai Mirror |date=2013-09-12 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref> The Union Urban Department Ministry brought the Mumbai Metro under the Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act of 1978 on 18 November 2013, thereby granting MMOPL the authority to fix fares. Prior to this notification, Blue Line

was under the Indian Tramways Act, 1886, and the Chief Minister had the sole power to decide fare revisions.<ref name="dnaindia6" /> In a letter to the state government dated 7 February, the Urban Development Ministry said, "MMOPL can fix the fare afresh after obtaining the recommendation of the Fare Fixation Committee (FFC). However, no FFC recommendation is necessary to fix the initial fare." Fare fixation is governed by relevant provisions of the Metro Railways (operations and maintenance) Act, 2002.<ref name="indiatimes4">{{cite web|agency=TNN |author=Manthan K. Mehta | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Fare-hike-likely-for-Versova-Ghatkopar-Metro/articleshow/34389616.cms |title=Fare hike likely for Versova-Ghatkopar Metro |work=The Times of India |date=29 April 2014 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> The Ministry's notification permits initial fare fixation without an FFC recommendation, but makes it mandatory for subsequent fare revisions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/mumbai-metro-may-start-soon-as-rinfra-allowed-to-fix-fares_1077643.html |title=Mumbai Metro may start soon as RInfra allowed to fix fares |website=Moneycontrol.com |date=30 April 2014 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

In an interview with ''DNA'' published on 9 May, MMRDA Commissioner U.P.S. Madan declared that the August 2013 fares were final stating, "There is already a fare notification in place about metro, which is final. The notification was issued recently with a revision in ticket prices. The fare notification is final and binding."<ref>{{cite web |author= |date=2014-05-09 |title=There's a fare notification on Metro and it's final: UPS Madan |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/interview-there-s-a-fare-notification-on-metro-and-it-s-final-ups-madan-1986391 |access-date=2014-05-26 |website=Daily News and Analysis}}</ref> Anil Galgali, an RTI activist and chairman of the Mumbai-based NGO Athak Seva Sangh, wrote a letter to the Chief Minister on 2 May 2014, urging him to use his special powers to prevent the fare hike. Galgali said, "The Maharashtra state government should use its special powers and stop the new fares from being implemented. The delay in project and increase in cost is not the fault of Mumbai's citizens. It is the responsibility of the Maharashtra state government to act against MMOPL's demands." He further accused the MMOPL of "blackmailing the government and playing with citizens".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/chavan-urged-to-stop-mumbai-metro-from-hiking-fares-114050201042_1.html |title=Chavan urged to stop Mumbai Metro from hiking fares |work=Business Standard |date=2014-05-02 |access-date=2014-05-26|agency=Press Trust of India }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/maharashtra-cm-urged-to-stop-mumbai-metro-from-hiking-fares/15268091 |title=Maharashtra CM urged to stop Mumbai Metro from hiking fares |website=Mid-day.com |date=2 May 2014 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> MMOPL announced the minimum and maximum fares on the line as {{INR}} 10 and {{INR}} 40 respectively in early May 2014.<ref name="timesofindia.indiatimes.com" /> However, MMOPL later announced a special introductory fare of {{INR}} 10, regardless of distance, for the first 30 days of service, i.e. from 8 June to 8 July.<ref name="livemint.com" />

On 9 June 2014, the MMRDA filed a case in the Bombay High Court seeking appointment of an arbitrator for the fare.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/High-court-to-take-up-Mumbai-Metro-fare-dispute-on-June-13/articleshow/36313676.cms|title=High court to take up Mumbai Metro fare dispute on June 13 | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=10 June 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/mumbai-metro-fare-hike-court-to-hear-case-on-friday/article23159028.ece|title=Mumbai Metro fare hike: Court to hear case on Friday|first=Rahul|last=Wadke|website=@businessline|date=9 June 2014 }}</ref>

==Stations==

{{Main|List of Mumbai Metro stations|l1=List of Mumbai Metro Stations}}
There are 12 stations on Blue Line. All stations have three levels that are accessed via stairs, escalators, and elevators. Trains leave from the second floor, which is the Platform level.<ref name="TOI1" /> There is a maximum gap of {{Cvt|85|mm}} between the platform and train doors.<ref name="mid-day6">{{cite web|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/making-sense-of-the-mumbai-metro/15226083 |title=Making sense of the Mumbai Metro |website=[[Mid-day]] |date=13 April 2014 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

There are 100 staircases (minimum 4 in each station), 45 elevators and 95 escalators on the 12 stations of Blue Line.<ref name="TOI1" /><ref name="mid-day6" /> Platforms have polycarbonate roofs which allow them to be naturally lit.<ref name="TOI1" /> Stations feature murals created by university students. Metro authorities organised the "Majhi Metro" festival and requested art and architecture students to enter a contest, where the winners were awarded the opportunity to design and style a metro station, based on the theme "Mumbai".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/murals-breathe-life-into-mumbai-metro-stations/article6095555.ece|title=Murals breathe life into Mumbai Metro stations|date=9 June 2014|work=[[The Hindu]]}}</ref>

On 3 July 2013, MMOPL announced that Wi-Fi services were enabled at all 12 stations on the line. The facility is expected to be available on moving trains by the end of the month. [[You Broadband]] is the service provider.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-offers-free-Wi-Fi-connectivity-at-all-stations/articleshow/37724325.cms|title=Metro offers free Wi-Fi connectivity at all stations | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=4 July 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-water-leakage-in-mumbai-metro-now-you-can-use-wi-fi-at-metro-stations-to-tweet-it-1999563|title=Water leakage in Mumbai metro? Now you can use Wi-Fi at metro stations to tweet it!|date=4 July 2014|website=[[Daily News and Analysis]]}}</ref>

There are no parking facilities available on Blue Line. The MMRDA said that this was because there was no space available.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.expressindia.com/latest-news/authority-mulls-parking-lots-at-upcoming-metro-stations/932336/ |title=Authority mulls parking lots at upcoming Metro stations |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |date=3 April 2012 |access-date=12 June 2012}}</ref> The Ghatkopar station is connected with the western side of the [[Ghatkopar railway station]] through a {{Convert|12|m|adj=on}} wide foot-over-bridge.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-ghatkopar-railway-station-to-soon-to-be-integrated-with-metro-station-1973677 |title=Ghatkopar railway station to soon to be integrated with metro station |website=[[Daily News and Analysis]] |date=2014-03-31 |access-date=2014-06-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://freepressjournal.in/commuters-sandwiched-between-mumbai-metro-and-railways/ |title=Commuters sandwiched between Mumbai Metro and railways |date=12 June 2014 |work=[[Free Press Journal]] |access-date=2014-06-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714182511/http://freepressjournal.in/commuters-sandwiched-between-mumbai-metro-and-railways/ |archive-date=14 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=7 June 2014 |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Andheri-Ghatkopar-stations-ill-prepared-for-commuter-surge/articleshow/36221743.cms |title=Andheri, Ghatkopar stations ill-prepared for commuter surge |work=The Times of India}}</ref>

Under sponsorship agreements, the MMOPL rebranded the Andheri and WEH stations as the Bank of Baroda Andheri station and the Magicbricks WEH station in August 2016 and February 2017 respectively. The MMRDA said that MMOPL cannot re-brand station's without its permission. In March 2017, the Union ministry of urban development clarified that MMOPL was permitted to rebrand stations. The revenue earned by MMOPL through the rebranding is not shared with the MMRDA, nor passed on to commuters through lower ticket fares.<ref>{{cite web|title=Centre okays rebranding of Mumbai Metro stations|url=http://www.asianage.com/metros/mumbai/150317/centre-okays-rebranding-of-mumbai-metro-stations.html|website=[[The Asian Age]]|access-date=16 March 2017|date=15 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Centre allows MMOPL to rebrand Metro stations|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/centre-allows-mmopl-to-rebrand-metro-stations-4569244/|website=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=16 March 2017|date=15 March 2017}}</ref>

As part of the Station Area Traffic Improvement Scheme (SATIS), the MMRDA moved all bus and taxi stands to a distance of about 40–50 metres away from the stations. The MMRDA believes that the previous location of the stands just next the stations resulted in traffic congestion and restricted the movement of pedestrians. Congestion issues were resolved after the implementation of SATIS at all stations on the line.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mumbai: MMRDA to make monorail corridor congestion free|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-mmrda-to-make-monorail-corridor-congestion-free/18143180|website=[[Mid-day]]|date=7 April 2017 |access-date=7 April 2017}}</ref>
