==Infrastructure==

===Rolling stock===
[[File:MumbaiMetroOne(747).jpg|thumb|A Mumbai Metro train in 2010]]
Six international firms - [[Siemens]], [[Bombardier Transportation|Bombardier]], [[Alstom]], [[Hyundai Rotem|Rotem-Hyundai]], [[CRRC Changchun Railway Vehicles|CNR Changchun]], and [[Nippon Sharyo]] - were shortlisted to provide rolling stock for the line,<ref>{{cite web|author=Chittaranjan Tembhekar |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mncs-eye-metro-rail-pie-1130143 | title=MNCs eye Metro Rail pie |publisher=DNA |date=2007-10-27 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref> but [[Nanjing Puzhen Rolling Stock Works|CSR Puzhen]] was ultimately chosen to supply rolling stock.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mumbai-metro.com/projec-update |title=Mumbai Metro One Project updates |website=mumbai-metro.com |access-date=2010-08-25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111118081246/http://www.mumbai-metro.com/projec-update |archive-date=18 November 2011}}</ref> CSR Puzhen was awarded a contract in May 2008 to supply 16 trains of 4 cars each for a total fee of {{INRConvert|6|b|year=2008}}. The first rake was shipped from [[Shanghai]] on 23 March 2010,<ref>[http://www.railwaygazette.com/nc/news/single-view/view/mumbais-beautiful-butterfly-emerges.html "Mumbai's beautiful butterfly emerges"]. [[Railway Gazette International]], 25 March 2010. Retrieved 24 October 2011.</ref> and the last rake arrived at Mumbai port by the end of February 2014.<ref name="dnaindia3" /><ref name="indiatimes3">{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbais-first-Metro-line-unlikely-to-meet-March-31-deadline/articleshow/31441109.cms |title=Mumbai's first Metro line unlikely to meet March 31 deadline |work=The Times of India |date=2014-03-05 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref>

Blue Line was allotted 64 coaches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Plans-to-add-44-more-coaches-to-first-Metro/Article1-862761.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120712083532/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Plans-to-add-44-more-coaches-to-first-Metro/Article1-862761.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 July 2012 |title=Plans to add 44 more coaches to first Metro |newspaper=Hindustan Times |access-date=12 June 2012}}</ref> Fourteen trains (of four cars) are in service during rush hour, and seven or eight in non-peak hours.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mumbai-metro-may-open-to-public-after-mid-may-1983827 |title=Mumbai Metro may open to public after mid-May |website=Daily News and Analysis |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> All coaches are [[air-conditioned]] and have [[humidity control]], and are designed to reduce noise and vibration.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/1829482/report-a-mumbai-metro-train-every-three-minutes |title=A Mumbai Metro train every three minutes |website=Daily News and Analysis |date=2013-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> Each coach is approximately {{convert|2.9|m|ftin}} wide<ref>{{cite web|last=Katkurwar |first=Saurabh |url=http://www.mid-day.com/news/2012/feb/260212-CIDCO-opts-for-wider-metro-coaches.htm |title=CIDCO opts for wider metro coaches |website=[[MiD DAY]] |date=26 February 2012 |access-date=28 March 2012}}</ref> and has 48 seats. A coach has a capacity of 375 passengers, and a single four car train has a total capacity of 1500 passengers. The coach body is made of lightweight stainless steel, with fire resistant metal doors. Coaches have metallic silver colour exteriors, and can be covered with vinyl sheets to display advertisements. The interior features anti-skid floors, and longitudinal seats with dedicated space to accommodate wheelchairs.<ref name="mid-day6" /> Trains on Blue Line are fitted with the VTS Firetide 7010 video transmission system.<ref name="mid-day3" /> Coaches are also fitted with [[LED display]]s showing dynamic route map, and [[LCD television|LCD TVs]] for entertainment, information and advertising. Windows in coaches are made of [[Insulated glazing|double glazed]] [[laminated glass]] to shut out noise. Each coach has eight externally hung, sliding bi-parting doors except the pilot cabin which has only 2. Doors are broad to enable wheelchair access. The maximum gap between the station platform and the doors is {{Cvt|85|mm}}.<ref name="mid-day6" /> Trains are outfitted with a number of features for safety and convenience, first-aid kits, fire-fighting equipment and intercom systems permitting communication with the train driver.<ref name="ToI70" /> Each coach contains a [[Train event recorder|black box]] to assist in accident investigations.<ref name="ToI70" />

[[File:Mumbai Metro Inside.jpg|left|thumb|Interiors of the Metro coach]]
The rolling stock is cleaned daily in an automated washing plant utilizing eco-friendly technology.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Green-technology-to-clean-Metro-in-Mumbai/articleshow/35690139.cms|title=Green technology to clean Metro in Mumbai | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=28 May 2014 }}</ref>

MMOPL initially used a Wheel Flange Lubrication (WFL) system to reduce wear and tear of rolling stock wheels. The agency invested {{INRConvert|30|c}} to introduce a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) chip based system to accomplish the task. The MMOPL said that the RFID system provides even longer lifespan for wheels, and the agency states that it will recover the {{INR}} 30 crore investment within 2 years through savings on maintenance costs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mumbai Metro uses RFID lubrication system to improve wheel maintenance {{!}} Latest News & Updates at Daily News & Analysis|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-mumbai-metro-uses-rfid-lubrication-system-to-improve-wheel-maintenance-2336958|website=dna|access-date=28 February 2017|date=27 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mumbai metro: One redesigns wheels to reduce wear and tear|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-metro-one-redesigns-wheels-to-reduce-wear-and-tear-4548861/|website=The Indian Express|access-date=2 March 2017|date=1 March 2017}}</ref>

===Power===
The [[ABB Group]] was awarded the contract for supplying power systems to Blue Line on 31 July 2008.<ref name="dnaindia5">{{cite web |author= |date=2008-08-01 |title=ABB gets Metro's first corridor |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-abb-gets-metro-s-first-corridor-1181048 |access-date=2014-03-27 |publisher=DNA}}</ref><ref name="Contracts">{{cite web|url=http://www.projectstoday.com/News/NewsDetails.aspx?smid=16&nid=22722|title=MMOPL awards contract to ABB, Siemens, SEW |work=Projects Today|date=8 January 2008|access-date=2010-01-15}}</ref> The line is electrified using [[25 kV AC railway electrification|25 kV AC]] at 50 Hz via [[overhead catenary]].

In early 2017, MMOPL completed the installation of light-emitting diode (LED) lighting at all metro stations, the depot, and administrative buildings to reduce electricity consumption. The MMOPL also began a project under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model to install rooftop solar panels at all stations and the metro depot. Under the model, a private company will bear the cost of setting and operating the panels, and will sell the generated power to the MMOPL at a rate of {{INR}} 5.1 per unit. A total of 2.30 MWp will be generated by the system, of which about 2 MWp is generated by the station's rooftop solar panels and 0.30 MWp is generated by the depot's solar panels. The LED lighting system and solar panels are estimated to reduce Blue Line's carbon emissions by 2,430 tons per year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mumbai's first metro to go green - Times of India|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mumbais-first-metro-to-go-green/articleshow/57920887.cms|website=The Times of India|date=30 March 2017 |access-date=30 March 2017}}</ref>

The MMOPL said that 30% of the total annual non-traction power requirement of approximately 11 MW would be met using solar power from May 2017. Solar energy powers the operation of station equipment such as lighting, air-conditioning, lifts, escalators and pumps.<ref>{{cite news|title=30 per cent of total power usage for Mumbai Metro from solar panels now|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/30-of-total-power-usage-for-metro-from-solar-panels-now/articleshow/58439960.cms|website=The Times of India|date=30 April 2017 |access-date=3 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Andheri, Ghatkopar Metro stations shine with solar panels|url=http://www.asianage.com/metros/mumbai/300417/andheri-ghatkopar-metro-stations-shine-with-solar-panels.html|website=Asian Age|access-date=3 May 2017|date=30 April 2017}}</ref>

===Signaling and communications===
Blue Line features an advanced [[railway signal|signaling]] system, including an automatic [[train protection system]] (ATPS) and automated signaling to control train movements.<ref name="Mummetro">{{cite web|url=http://www.mmrdamumbai.org/|title=Mumbai Metro project|publisher=[[MMRDA]]|date=1 January 2008|access-date=2010-01-01}}</ref> Siemens supplied the signalling and train control systems required for the project,<ref name="dnaindia5" /> while [[Thales Group|Thales]] supplied the communication systems. The network's signaling and train control systems are based on LZB 700M technology.<ref name="Contracts" />

=== Bridges ===
[[File:Metro Bridge.jpg|thumb|right|The [[cable-stayed]] metro bridge over the [[Western Express Highway]] in [[Andheri]].]]
Blue Line contains a 1284-metre steel bridge, modeled on the [[Howrah Bridge]] in [[Kolkata]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mid-day.com/news/2012/feb/060212-Howrah-Bridge-coming-soon-to-Andheri.htm|title='Howrah Bridge' coming soon to Andheri}}</ref> crossing the [[Western Line (Mumbai Suburban Railway)|Western Line]] at [[Andheri]]. The bridge was constructed in 2012. It cost {{INRConvert|350|m|year=2012}}.<ref name="TOI5">{{cite news| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-ride-in-June-13-Work-on-crucial-bridge-completed/articleshow/17761691.cms | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928194223/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2012-12-26/mumbai/36007202_1_metro-bridge-mumbai-metro-one-pvt-cable-stay-bridge | url-status=live | archive-date=2013-09-28 | work=[[The Times of India]] | title=Metro ride in June '13? Work on crucial bridge completed}}</ref> The bridge, which was initially planned to be made of concrete, was constructed of steel by [[Braithwaite Burn & Jessop Construction Company]] (BBJ), Kolkata, who also fabricated the Howrah Bridge. The steel girders were pre-fabricated at BBJ's Heavy Plant Yard in [[Kolkata]]. The bridge was then disassembled and transported over the course of a week to the site.<ref name="TOI5" />

Another notable bridge on Blue Line is the 175-metre-long cable-stayed bridge over the Andheri Flyover on the [[Western Express Highway]]. The Andheri flyover is 13 metres above ground level, and the metro line travels 6.5 metres above it. The bridge is 39 metres above the ground at its highest point. Construction on the bridge started in mid-2009 and was completed on 24 August 2012. The bridge was built by MMOPL, with Switzerland-based [[Vorspann System Losinger|VSL International Limited]] as its partners.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131005223358/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Metro-marvel-Cable-stayed-bridge-complete/Article1-919506.aspx Metro marvel: Cable-stayed bridge complete - Hindustan Times]</ref>

===Wastewater treatment===
On 1 October 2012, [[Xylem Inc.|Xylem]], a water technology provider based in the United States, announced that it had been awarded a contract to develop wastewater treatment and recycling systems for the [[Mumbai Metro]]. The value of the contract was undisclosed. The system will incorporate a 1.2-million-litre-capacity sewage treatment plant with wastewater recycling capabilities; trials of the plant were expected to be commissioned by late November 2012. The plant will be equipped with Xylem's Sanitaire wastewater treatment technology, which is expected to help save up to 1.2 million litres of water a day.<ref>[http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/article3955565.ece "Xylem bags Mumbai metro rail contract for wastewater treatment"]. ''Business Line''. 1 October 2012.</ref>

==Operations==
Lines on the Mumbai Metro are currently identified by numbers. In March 2016, MMRDA Metropolitan Commissioner, U.P.S. Madan, announced that all lines on the system would be colour coded after more lines were opened. Blue Line is generally depicted in blue in most maps, including on maps onboard Blue Line trains, leading to speculation that the line would be renamed the Blue Line when the colour coding is announced.

===Operator===
[[File:Logo of Mumbai Metro Line 1.svg|thumb|Logo of MMOPL, the special purpose vehicle (SPV) that operates Blue Line 1]]

The contract for the Versova–Andheri–Ghatkopar corridor (Blue Line 1) was awarded in March 2007 to Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL), a [[special purpose vehicle]] (SPV) formed specifically to implement the project. MMOPL was promoted as a [[Public–private partnerships in India|public–private partnership]] with equity participation from [[Reliance Infrastructure]] (69%), the [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority]] (MMRDA) (26%), and [[Veolia Transport]] (5%).<ref>{{cite news|agency=Press Trust of India |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/news-by-industry/transportation/railways/mumbai-metro-closer-to-operations-to-get-speed-certificate-this-week/articleshow/32545604.cms |title=Mumbai Metro closer to operations, to get speed certificate this week |work=The Economic Times |date=2014-03-23 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref> Veolia's stake has since been transferred to [[RATP Dev Transdev Asia]]. RATP Dev Transdev Asia later sold its 5% stake to MMOPL, resulting in Reliance Infrastructure increasing its shareholding to 74%.<ref>{{cite news |title=Metro-1 R-Infra buyout: MMRDA denies info on valuation report |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/metro-1-r-infra-buyout-mmrda-denies-info-on-valuation-report/articleshow/109481756.cms |work=The Times of India |date=12 May 2024 |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=State cabinet clears proposal to buy Metro-1 from Anil Ambani |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/state-cabinet-clears-proposal-to-buy-metro-1-from-anil-ambani-101710183714636.html |work=Hindustan Times |date=24 May 2024 |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref>

While MMOPL is the project owner and asset operator, day-to-day train operations were contracted to Metro One Operation Pvt Ltd (MOOPL), a separate joint venture between Reliance Infrastructure (30%) and RATP Dev Transdev Asia (70%), under a 5-year operations and maintenance agreement.<ref name=ratp>{{cite web|url=https://www.ratp.fr/en/groupe-ratp/metrotrains/metro-one-operation-pvt-ltd-moopl|title=Metro One Operation Pvt. Ltd. (MOOPL)|publisher=RATP|access-date=1 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201102018/https://www.ratp.fr/en/groupe-ratp/metrotrains/metro-one-operation-pvt-ltd-moopl|archive-date=1 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

MMOPL is designated as the Metro Railway Administrator under the ''[[Metro Railway (Operations and Maintenance) Act, 2002]]''. Although this legally requires RTI compliance, a workaround has been implemented where RTI requests for Blue Line 1 can be routed through the MMRDA, similar to the model used for [[Rapid Metro Gurgaon]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Binoo Nair |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-reliance-s-versova-andheri-mumbai-metro-won-t-come-under-rti-1991211 |title=Reliance's Versova-Andheri Mumbai Metro won't come under RTI |website=Daily News and Analysis |date=26 May 2014 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

The initial 5-year contract to operate and maintain the metro expired on 7 June 2019. MMOPL expressed its intent to extend this contract beyond the initial term.<ref>{{cite web|title=RInfra, Veolia to extend partnership beyond Mumbai Metro|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-rinfra-veolia-to-extend-partnership-beyond-mumbai-metro-2407140|website=dna|access-date=3 May 2017|date=19 April 2017}}</ref>

In April 2017, MMOPL partnered with [[Google]] to provide real-time train schedules and indoor station maps via [[Google Maps]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mumbai commute: Google Maps mobile app to help you avoid traffic on your way to Metro|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/mumbai-commute-google-maps-mobile-app-to-help-you-avoid-traffic-on-your-way-to-metro/story-Sfws4nfodwJGKnrIcv6eHL.html|website=Hindustan Times|access-date=3 May 2017|language=en|date=21 April 2017}}</ref>

Following the [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in India]], operations were suspended in March 2020. In August 2020, MMOPL informed MMRDA of its intention to divest its stake, citing financial losses.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Venkatraman |first1=Tanushree |title=Amid losses, RInfra writes to Maharashtra govt for selling Mumbai Metro-1 stakes |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/amid-losses-rinfra-writes-to-maharashtra-govt-for-selling-mumbai-metro-1-stakes/story-NQ1B9dtqTAG0KTICq5GozN.html |access-date=21 August 2020 |work=Hindustan Times |date=21 August 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

===Fare collection===
The minimum and maximum fares on the line are {{INR}} 10 and {{INR}} 40 respectively, roughly 1.5 times the current unsubsidized BEST bus fare for a given distance.<ref name="timesofindia.indiatimes.com">{{cite web |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-ride-will-cost-Rs-10-to-Rs-40-on-VAG-corridor/articleshow/34937669.cms |title=Metro ride will cost Rs 10 to Rs 40 on VAG corridor |work=The Times of India |date=2014-05-10 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref> Blue Line utilizes an Automatic Fare Collection System (AFC).<ref name="TOI1" /> The contract for the fare collection system was awarded to Spain's [[Indra Sistemas]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mumbai Metro to run in 30 months, awards major contracts |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/mumbai-metro-to-run-in-30-months-awards-major-contracts/articleshow/3500164.cms?from=mdr |access-date=29 October 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=18 September 2008}}</ref> Riders can pay their fare using tokens, reloadable smart cards or by through [[QR code payment]]. Smart cards can be recharged online.<ref>{{cite web |author=Ateeq Shaikh |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-metro-one-plans-online-smart-card-recharge-1984190 |title=Metro One plans online smart card recharge |website=Daily News and Analysis |date=2014-05-02 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

From 19 June 2014, the MMOPL introduced an off-peak fare of {{INR}} 5 on Blue Line. The fare applies between any two stations, regardless of distance, from 5:30am to 8:00am on weekdays.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/metro-gets-cheaper-peak-hours-701 |title=Metro gets cheaper in off-peak hours |date=19 June 2014 |work=The Asian Age |access-date=2014-06-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140619115720/http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/metro-gets-cheaper-peak-hours-701 |archive-date=19 June 2014}}</ref> The relevant token must be purchased during off-peak hours and used within half an hour of purchase. Smartcards automatically deduct the lower fare if a commuter uses his card to exit the metro during off-peak hours.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/City/Mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-introduces-off-peak-hour-rates/articleshow/36766047.cms |title=Mumbai Metro introduces off-peak-hour rates |author=Manthan K Mehta |date=18 June 2014 |work=The Times of India}}</ref> Approximately 55% of commuters on the line, pay using smart cards as of June 2015.<ref name="autogenerated6">{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-8th-densest-network-in-the-world/articleshow/47571058.cms|title=Mumbai Metro 8th densest network in the world | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=7 June 2015 }}</ref>

From January 2017, passengers can also purchase tickets on their phone and enter the gates by means of QR code payment. The service is provided by [[Paytm]] and a QR code is generated on the commuter's phone which is read at entry and exit by a scanner at the turnstiles.<ref name="qrpay">{{cite news |title=Paytm introduces QR-based metro tickets for Mumbaikars |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/paytm-metro-ticketing-window-fare-pass-qr-code-metro-line-mumbaikar/story/264271.html |access-date=17 November 2018 |work=Business Insider |date=17 November 2017}}</ref> In January 2020, MMOPL started issuing paper tickets with a QR code printed on it with an aim to completely move from the earlier plastic RFID-based tokens.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mumbai: Metro One launches Paper QR ticket from today |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mumbai-metro-one-launches-paper-qr-ticket-from-today |access-date=4 February 2020 |work=Free Press Journal |date=16 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> The same month, it launched an unlimited trip pass that could be purchased as an add-on to an existing trip pass.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mehta |first1=Manthank |title=Unlimited-ride Metro passes from today |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mumbai-unlimited-ride-metro-passes-from-today/articleshow/73535748.cms |access-date=4 February 2020 |work=The Times of India |date=23 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In November 2022, MMOPL began allowing passengers to purchase tickets through [[WhatsApp]]. Passengers can text "Hi" to 967000 8889 to receive a link through which they can complete the ticket purchase, and ultimately receive a QR code that serves as the ticket.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |last2= |last3= |first3= |title=Purchase your Mumbai Metro ticket without going to the counter |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/purchase-your-mumbai-metro-ticket-without-going-to-the-counter/articleshow/95725905.cms |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=The Times of India |date= 24 November 2022|language=en}}</ref>

In December 2023, MMOPL began accepting the [[National Common Mobility Card]] (NCMC) at all metro stations.<ref>{{cite news |title=Metro commuters can now use one card for ride on three lines |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/metro-commuters-can-now-use-one-card-for-ride-on-three-lines-101702581198609.html |access-date=25 February 2025 |work=Hindustan Times |date=15 December 2023 |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Frequency===
Services operate on Blue Line for 18.5 hours everyday (5:30 AM to midnight). Headway on the line is 3 minutes during peak hours and 5 minutes during non-peak hours (11:30am and 4:30pm).<ref>{{cite web |title=Mumbai Metro every 5 minutes during non-peak hours from Monday |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/mumbai-metro-every-5-minutes-during-non-peak-hours-from-monday/story-JyOZvGNpSTgwjnjAfLeimJ.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=9 October 2018 |language=en |date=21 September 2018}}</ref>

Station dwell time is 30 seconds.<ref name="TOI1"/> Blue Line has a high rate of punctuality with 99.99% of trains arriving on time.<ref name="65kmphspeed"/>

===Ridership===
A metro train has four coaches and an overall capacity of 1500 passengers (375 per coach).<ref name="ReferenceC"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/mumbai-metro-to-begin-operations-on-sunday-114060700219_1.html|title=Mumbai Metro to begin operations on Sunday|first=Sanjay|last=Jog|date=7 June 2014|work=Business Standard}}</ref> The seating capacity of every coach alternates between 48 and 52, of which 4 seats in each coach are reserved for senior citizens and handicapped commuters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbais-first-metro-to-be-open-for-public-on-sunday/|title=Flag off: Mumbai becomes a Metro today|date=8 June 2014}}</ref> From 15 August 2014, following demands by female commuters, 32 of 48 seats in the Versova-end coach of every four coach train is reserved for women. These seats are part of a reserved space for women which is separated from the rest of the coach by a strip separator and can accommodate 150 passengers, including standees. Male children under the age of 12, who are accompanied by female passengers, are permitted in the reserved space.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mumbaimirror.indiatimes.com/mumbai/other/Metro-coaches-to-have-reserved-space-for-women/articleshow/40219304.cms|title=Metro coaches to have reserved space for women|website=Mumbai Mirror}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/From-Friday-1-Metro-coach-to-be-reserved-for-women/articleshow/40205410.cms|title=From Friday, 1 Metro coach to be reserved for women | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=13 August 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Metro-greets-women-commuters-with-32-reserved-seats-in-last-coach/articleshow/40618323.cms|title=Metro greets women commuters with 32 reserved seats in last coach | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=22 August 2014 }}</ref> Prior to the introduction of the reserved space, 6 seats per coach had been reserved for women.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://freepressjournal.in/exclusive-metro-coach-for-women/ |title=Exclusive Metro coach for women - Free Press Journal |website=freepressjournal.in |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814171922/http://freepressjournal.in/exclusive-metro-coach-for-women/ |archive-date=2014-08-14}}</ref>

Blue Line transported 200 million passengers within 786 days of operations. It crossed the 250 million mark on 11 February, or within 957 days, the fastest time in which any metro in India has reached the milestone.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>

The maximum ridership recorded on a single day was 312,215 and minimum was 64,522 till January 2019.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mumbai Metro Ridership - RTI Reply|url=http://blog.onlinerti.com/2015/06/12/mumbai-metro-ridership-and-service-distruption/|work=OnlineRTI}}</ref> In early January 2019, a strike by BEST staffers saw a spike in the ridership of the Metro and the [[Mumbai Monorail|Monorail]]. Daily ridership crossed 500,000 for four consecutive days with an average increase of 55,000 per day with ridership touching 520,000 on 11 January.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mehta |first1=Manthan K |title=Mumbai: BEST strike pushes daily Metro ridership over 5 lakh for first time |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mumbai-best-strike-pushes-daily-metro-ridership-over-5-lakh-for-first-time/articleshow/67533513.cms |access-date=29 January 2019 |work=The Times of India|date=15 January 2019}}</ref>

Growth of ridership on the corridor slowed down in 2019 when the BEST undertaking slashed its minimum fares to ₹5 for up to {{convert|5|km|mi}}.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rao |first1=Shashank |title=Mumbai: Metro riders rush to BEST rate again |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mumbai-metro-riders-rush-to-best-rate-again-2793369 |access-date=21 August 2020 |work=DNA India |date=30 September 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

===Speed===
The RDSO Chief Engineer Ajay Kumar Verma initially permitted a maximum speed of only {{Cvt|50|km/h}}. "These tracks have been constructed based on European standards but we follow Indian Railway standards. The two have differences on several technical parameters, including the tolerance limit of tracks and even curves," said a railway official.<ref name="mid-day2" /> The slower speed added around 7 minutes to the journey time.<ref name="mid-day2" /> Another reason why trains on the line operate at slower speeds is because stations are only {{Cvt|800 to 1000|m}} apart, which prevents trains from picking up speed.<ref name="mid-day2">{{cite web|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbais-superfast-metros-will-only-run-at-50-kmph-for-now/15146067 |title=Mumbai's 'superfast' metros will only run at 50 km/h for now |website=Mid-day.com |date=2014-03-09 |access-date=2014-03-27}}</ref>

Trains began operating at speeds of {{Cvt|65|km/h}} from 24 March 2016. The increase is not expected to significantly reduce travel time on the line due to the low inter-station distance. The Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS) granted approval to operate at speeds up to {{Cvt|80|km/h}}, and RDSO gave its clearance on 18 November 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/metro-run-faster-24th-748|title=Metro to run faster from 24th|first=Mehul R.|last=Thakkar|date=23 March 2016|website=The Asian Age}}</ref> The MMRDA plans to further increase the operating speed to that limit after training metro pilots to operate trains at higher speeds.<ref name="65kmphspeed">{{cite web|last1=Mishra|first1=Kamal|title=Mumbai Metro runs at a faster speed now - Mumbai Mirror -|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/mumbai/others/Mumbai-Metro-runs-at-a-faster-speed-now/articleshow/51588777.cms|website=Mumbai Mirror|access-date=9 April 2016}}</ref>

===Security===
In a statement on released 13 December 2013, MMOPL announced, "Trained sniffer dogs will patrol each of the stations. There will be security guards in civilian dress who will intermingle with the public to check for any suspicious activity outside and inside the station premises." Security is provided by private security guards deployed by MMOPL and the Maharashtra State Security Corporation.<ref name="dnaindia.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-metro-rail-to-have-sniffer-dog-bomb-detection-squads-1934894 |title=Metro rail to have sniffer dog, bomb detection squads |publisher=DNA |date=2013-12-14 |access-date=2014-02-06}}</ref>

Other security measures on Blue Line include metal detectors,<ref name="mid-day6" /> security cameras, frisking each passenger, and running their luggage through X-ray scanners.<ref name="dnaindia.com" /> All stations are fitted with fire alarm systems and fire safety devices, and trains have fire resistant metal doors.<ref name="mid-day6" /> Passengers are prohibited from carrying luggage measuring more than 2 ft x 1.5 ft on the metro.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/home/city/Airport-station-to-bear-brunt-of-Metro-ban-on-heavy-bags/articleshow/34445384.cms |title=Airport station to bear brunt of Metro ban on heavy bags |work=Mumbai Mirror |date=2014-05-01 |access-date=2014-05-26}}</ref>

Stations are actively monitored by security personnel. A senior metro official explained, "The trained unit will keep an eye in the vicinity of Metro stations in plain clothes, posing as common men. The unit will be on the lookout for mischievous activities in Metro stations by miscreants and take necessary action. Depending on the kind and level of trouble and threat posed by such people, action will be taken against them. Senior security personnel will take a call if these persons can be punished or penalised under the Central Metro Act, or should be handed over to the local police for necessary action."<ref>{{cite web|author=Anand Mishra |url=http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/mmopl-says-it-has-robust-security-set-metro-rail-328 |title=MMOPL says it has robust security set up for Metro rail |work=The Asian Age |date=2014-05-16 |access-date=2014-05-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520220253/http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/mmopl-says-it-has-robust-security-set-metro-rail-328 |archive-date=20 May 2014}}</ref>

Following an incident on the mostly underground [[Kolkata Metro Blue Line]] on 23 June 2014, where a non-AC metro train carrying passengers developed a glitch and got stuck inside a tunnel for an hour and a half, Mumbai Metro officials commented that their system has an emergency evacuation plan in place. An MMOPL spokesperson said, "The evacuation process will take two minutes if passengers are asked to alight midsection and 7–10 minutes if the train has to be taken to the nearest station."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-has-plan-for-evacuation/articleshow/37100473.cms|title=Mumbai Metro has 'plan' for evacuation | Mumbai News - Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=23 June 2014 }}</ref>

==Retail and advertising==
In December 2013, Times Innovative Media OOH acquired the advertising rights on Blue Line for a period of 15 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/times-ooh-unveils-advt-sponsorship-options-at-mumbai-metro-114021201362_1.html |title=Times OOH unveils advt, sponsorship options at Mumbai Metro |work=Business Standard |date=2014-02-12 |access-date=2014-03-27|agency=Press Trust of India }}</ref>

All 12 stations on the line have [[food and beverage]] shops, convenience stores, and ATMs. Some stations have mobile accessories stores.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/metro-commuters-can-shop-on-the-move-stations-to-get-retail-outlets/|title=Metro commuters can shop on the move, stations to get retail outlets|date=6 June 2014}}</ref> Lite Bite Foods Pvt Ltd (LBF) was awarded the food and beverage concessions across all stations on Blue Line. LBF supports these outlets from their 6,400 sq ft commissary near the international airport.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hospitalitybizindia.com/detailNews.aspx?aid=19010&sid=1 |title=Lite Bite Foods awarded F&B concessions for Mumbai Metro 1 |work=Hospitality Biz India |date=2014-03-19 |access-date=2014-03-27 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140324111428/http://www.hospitalitybizindia.com/detailNews.aspx?aid=19010&sid=1 |archive-date=24 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fnbnews.com/article/detnews.asp?articleid=35210&sectionid=1 |title=Lite Bite Foods awarded food & beverage concessions for Mumbai Metro 1 |work=Food & Beverage News |date=2014-03-14 |access-date=2014-03-27 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140324112237/http://www.fnbnews.com/article/detnews.asp?articleid=35210&sectionid=1 |archive-date=24 March 2014}}</ref>

Stations on the line have special [[Domino's Pizza]] outlets that can serve pizzas within 3–5 minutes of ordering, much faster than a typical outlet's 10–15 minutes. The outlets use turbo ovens and pizza warmers to reduce the time for preparation. The outlets also have glass windows through which customers can view their pizza being made. The outlets only serve pizzas of one specific size. The first such [[Jubilant FoodWorks|Domino's Pizza outlet in India]] was opened at Chakala station in June 2015. Andheri and Versova were the next to receive such outlets, with plans to expand it to all stations on the line.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ultra.news/d-r/11407/dominos-to-offer-pizzas-on-mumbai-metro-in-3-5-minutes|title=Domino's to offer 'Turbo Pizza' on Mumbai Metro|date=5 June 2015}}</ref>

Blue Line 1 is a rapid transit metro line of the Mumbai Metro, in the city of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. The 11.40 km (7.08 mi) line is fully elevated and consists of 12 stations, from Versova to Ghatkopar. The line connects the eastern and western suburbs of Mumbai. It was built at an estimated cost of ₹4,321 crore (US$450 million) and is operated by the Metro One Operation Pvt. Ltd (MOOPL) on a 5-year contract. This special purpose vehicle, namely, Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (Mumbai Metro 1), was incorporated for the implementation of the project. Reliance Infrastructure holds 74% of the equity share capital of MMOPL, 26% is with the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA).
The Mumbai Metro 1 Blue Line started operations on 8 June 2014. It has the eighth-highest passenger density of any metro line in the world. The Blue Line has the steepest curve of any metro line in India. There are a total of 64 curves on the line, with the steepest curve being 107 metres (351 ft).
